## Simple explanation

Feature engineering is the process of turning raw data into inputs that
help a model solve a task. It may involve combining, transforming, or
selecting variables.

## Technical explanation

Feature engineering includes domain-informed transformations such as
normalization, date decomposition, categorical encoding, interaction
terms, and aggregation. Transformations should be fitted without leaking
held-out information and applied consistently in training and serving.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Good features can expose useful structure to a model, reduce noise, and
improve performance. Feature pipelines also create maintenance and
consistency obligations when data distributions or product logic change.

## How it works

Understand the task and available data, create candidate transformations,
evaluate them with a leakage-safe validation strategy, and package useful
transformations into a reproducible pipeline. Monitor feature availability
and distributions after deployment.

## Practical example

A transaction timestamp can be transformed into hour of day and day of
week. These features may help a fraud model capture temporal patterns,
provided the information is available at prediction time.

## Common misconceptions

- Feature engineering is not always manual; models can learn
  representations from raw data.
- A feature that correlates with the target may be a leakage signal rather
  than a valid predictor.
- Adding many engineered features can increase complexity and overfitting.
